plans.title: Compliance plans

cash.body: Invoicing, reminders and calls in US business hours, payables ready for your approval, a weekly cash report.

order.title: Order desk
order.body: Order entry, 3PL releases, shipping documents, delivery tracking and returns.

weekly.title: What you'll see every week
weekly.intro: A short cash report every Monday and a one-page scorecard every quarter. The numbers come from your own books.

dont.title: What we don't do
dont.intro: Our limits are in writing. Trust starts there.

i1.title: We never act as importer of record.
i1.body: The record stays with your company. We audit it and report what is missing.

i2.title: We never hold or move your money.
i2.body: Customer payments go straight to your account. We prepare payables; you approve and release them from your own bank.

i3.title: Your licensed customs broker files all customs entries.
i3.body: Your broker prepares and files everything that goes to CBP. We help you gather the information your broker asks for.

i4.title: We never use virtual-office addresses.
i4.body: Our address is a real business address. CBP no longer accepts a registered-agent or business-center address on Form 5106 either.

i5.title: Collections run in your name, and accounts more than 90 days late go to a licensed agency.
i5.body: Your customer relationships stay yours. Accounts past 90 days go to an agency licensed for that work.

data.title: How your data is protected

d4.title: Section 7216 consent

d5.title: A clear line on AI

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: Will you act as our importer of record?
faq.a1: No. We never act as importer of record. We audit your record and help you gather the information your broker asks for.
faq.q2: Do you file customs entries or CBP refund requests?
faq.a2: No. Your licensed customs broker prepares and files all customs entries and CBP refund requests.
faq.a3: No. Customer payments go straight to your account. We prepare payables; you approve them and release them from your own bank.
faq.q4: Whose name do collections run in?
faq.a4: Yours. Accounts more than 90 days late go to a licensed collection agency.
faq.a5: Collections calls run 8:00-16:00 US Eastern. We answer you in Turkish, and the first reply comes within 1 business day.
faq.a6: The check report arrives in 10 business days. A plan or desk starts once the engagement letter is signed.
faq.q7: Do we need to enter our tax ID on the site?
faq.a7: No. This site never asks for tax ID numbers, EINs or financial documents. Documents come through a secure channel after you sign.

riskTest.title: US risk test
riskTest.intro: 10 questions. Yes/no answers and ranges only. No tax IDs, no documents.
riskTest.autoAdvance: Tapping an answer moves you to the next question.

usEntity.text: Do you have a US-registered company (LLC or corporation)?

ior.text: Is your company the importer of record on goods shipped to the US?
ior.help: If your US customer imports in its own name, choose No.

iorAddress.text: Is the address on your importer record (Form 5106) a registered-agent, virtual-office or business-center address?

brokerCheck.text: Has your customs broker checked your importer record against the new address rule since September 18, 2026?

form5472.text: Has Form 5472 been filed for your US company every year?
form5472.help: Form 5472 is the IRS form foreign-owned US companies use to report related-party transactions.

salesStates.text: How many US states do you sell into?

taxRegs.text: In how many states are you registered for sales tax?

paymentDays.text: On average, how many days do your US customers take to pay?

followUp.text: Does someone follow up on your US receivables during US business hours?

refundBank.text: Do you have a US bank account on file in ACE for CBP refunds (ACH)?
refundBank.help: Since February 6, 2026, CBP issues refunds electronically only.

result.title: Your result
result.lowBody: Your answers show no clear gap. Checking the rules once a year is still a good habit.
result.mediumBody: A few areas have gaps. One check usually clears them up.
result.highBody: At least one area carries a direct penalty or cancellation risk. We suggest a short call to set priorities.
result.informational: This result is informational; it is not legal, tax or customs advice.
result.emailBody: We'll send your result and the sources for each issue.

form5472Missing.title: Missing Form 5472 years
form5472Missing.body: The IRS penalty is $25,000 for each Form 5472 not filed, per year. If 90 days pass after an IRS notice, another $25,000 is added for each 30 days.

form5472Unknown.title: Form 5472 status unclear
form5472Unknown.body: Knowing which years were filed is the first step. Each missing year carries a $25,000 penalty.

iorAddress.title: Importer record address
iorAddress.body: Since September 18, 2026, CBP can void an importer number whose Form 5106 address is a registered agent, P.O. box or business center.

iorUnknown.title: Importer record unclear
iorUnknown.body: Without knowing who holds the record and what address it uses, you can't prepare for the new rules.

brokerCheck.title: No broker check yet
brokerCheck.body: Confirm with your broker that your record meets the new address rule. New importer requirements are being prepared under EO 14411.

salesTaxGap.title: Sales-tax gap
salesTaxGap.body: Since Wayfair (2018), a state can require you to collect its sales tax once your sales there pass its threshold, even with no physical presence. Each state you sell into without registering is a possible gap.

salesTaxUnknown.title: Sales-tax registrations unclear
salesTaxUnknown.body: Knowing where you are registered is the first step to closing gaps.

paymentDays.title: Long payment days
paymentDays.body: Every 10 days you cut from average payment days frees cash equal to about 2.7% of your annual US sales.

noFollowUp.title: No follow-up in US hours
noFollowUp.body: Istanbul is 7-8 hours ahead of US Eastern. Without someone following up in US hours, payment questions wait until the next day.

refundBank.title: No bank account for CBP refunds
refundBank.body: CBP pays refunds only by ACH to a US bank account, and it holds IEEPA refunds for importers with no bank details on file in ACE.

refundUnknown.title: Refund account unclear
refundUnknown.body: Ask your broker whether ACH details are on file in ACE. Without them, refunds are held.

calculators.title: See it in numbers
calculators.intro: Two quick calculations. Your numbers stay in your browser; they are sent only if you ask us to email the result.

cash.title: Cash freed by faster collections
cash.formula: Formula: annual US sales / 365 x (current days - target days)
cash.example: Example: {sales} in sales, from 62 days down to 40: about {result}.
cash.note: This is arithmetic, not a promise.
cash.invalid: Target days must be lower than current days.

form5472.title: Form 5472 penalty exposure
form5472.continuation: If 90 days pass after an IRS notice, another {penalty} is added for each 30 days, with no cap.
form5472.multiple: With more than one related party, each needs its own form.

about.title: We carry Turkish companies west
about.nameBody1: On the Mediterranean sailors' wind rose, the west is ponente. Turkish sailors call it günbatısı, where the sun sets.
about.nameBody2: Ponenti carries Turkish companies west, to the United States.
about.founderP1: I'm {name}. I grew up with Turkish and English, and I've spent my career in US finance and trade operations.
about.founderP2: I kept seeing Turkish companies hit the same problems on the US side: filings run late, sales tax stays open in several states, US customers pay late, and follow-up happens by email from Istanbul.
about.founderP3: Ponenti exists to run that work at one desk, in Turkish, during US business hours.
about.bio: Bilingual in Turkish and English. Former UPS financial analyst and Senior Manager of Go-to-Market Strategy (pricing, revenue management, FP&A). Hands-on in bookkeeping and month-end close, B2B invoicing and collections, sales-tax filings, and customs entries with licensed brokers.
about.how1: Every client has one owner and a written deadline calendar.
about.how3: The numbers come from your own books: a cash report every week, a scorecard every quarter.
about.how4: Our limits are in writing: we're not your importer of record, we don't hold your money, and your broker files customs entries.
about.first10Intro: This is how the US back-office check runs.
about.step1: Intro call and document list. We ask for documents through a secure upload link, never as email attachments.
about.step2: Importer record: address, owners, bond and broker authorization. Filing history.
about.step3: Sales-tax exposure by state. Receivables aging and average payment days.
about.step4: Penalty exposure in dollars, a fix plan and a quote.
about.step5: Results call: the report, the priorities and the quote.
about.data2: The team: only the people assigned to your file. Before any access from outside the US, we get your signed Section 7216 consent.
about.data3: Return review and e-filing: a US accounting firm under contract.
about.data4: Software: business accounts with two-factor login. AI only on business plans that bar training.
about.data5: No one else: we don't sell your data or share it for marketing.
